Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between two Markov chains

Source: R/chainComparison.R
divergenceRate.Rd

Computes the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate of a Markov chain x from a Markov chain y on the same states: the limit of \(\frac{1}{n} D(X_1,\ldots,X_n \,\|\, Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)\), the average information per step for discriminating x against y.

Usage

divergenceRate(x, y, weights = NULL, base = exp(1))

Arguments

x, y

Two markovchain objects with the same states, matched by name.

weights

Optional non-negative numeric vector, one entry per state (named or in the order of states(x)), with which the row divergences are averaged; it is normalized to sum to one. The default, NULL, uses the stationary distribution of x, which must then be unique.

base

The base of the logarithm: the default exp(1) gives the rate in nats, 2 in bits.

Value

A single non-negative number, Inf when x makes with positive probability a transition that y forbids from a state of positive weight.

Details

For chains with transition matrices \(P\) (of x) and \(Q\) (of y) and with \(\pi\) the stationary distribution of \(P\), the divergence rate is $$D(P \,\|\, Q) = \sum_i \pi_i \sum_j P_{ij} \log \frac{P_{ij}}{Q_{ij}},$$ which Rached, Alajaji and Campbell (2004) prove to be the limit above for irreducible chains, whatever the initial distributions. By the ergodic theorem it is also the almost sure limit of \(\frac1n \log \frac{\Pr_P(X_1, \ldots, X_n)}{\Pr_Q(X_1, \ldots, X_n)}\) along a path of x. It is zero exactly when the rows of \(P\) and \(Q\) agree on every state of positive weight, and it is not symmetric.

With weights equal to the relative frequencies of the departure states of a sequence, \(2N D(\hat P \,\|\, Q)\), with \(N\) the number of transitions, is the likelihood-ratio statistic \(G^2\) of the hypothesis that the sequence comes from \(Q\) (Kullback, Kupperman and Ku 1962), as computed by verifyEmpiricalToTheoretical.

References

Rached, Z., Alajaji, F. and Campbell, L. L. (2004). The Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov sources. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 50(5), 917-921. doi:10.1109/TIT.2004.826687

Kullback, S., Kupperman, M. and Ku, H. H. (1962). Tests for contingency tables and Markov chains. Technometrics, 4(4), 573-608.

See also

compareChains, entropyRate

Examples

s <- c("a", "b", "c")
P <- new("markovchain", states = s, transitionMatrix = matrix(
  c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.6, 0.3, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5), 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(s, s)))
Q <- new("markovchain", states = s, transitionMatrix = matrix(
  c(0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1, 0.6), 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(s, s)))
divergenceRate(P, Q)
#> [1] 0.05428363
divergenceRate(Q, P) # not symmetric
#> [1] 0.05065658
divergenceRate(P, P)
#> [1] 0
